name: Cheese pashtida — base recipe (פשטידת גבינות)

source.author: Instagram — rotemnisim (Hebrew, "healthy & balanced recipes" series)
source.notes: A bare cheese-custard pashtida (no vegetables in the base ingredient list) — eggs + 4 cheeses bound with a little flour/baking powder, baked. The post explicitly offers optional veg add-ins (onion, oregano, broccoli, corn, spinach, etc.) but doesn't fix amounts, so this entry is the BASE as listed. Method caption was cut off after '180°C, top-bottom heat' — baked similarly to the other egg-cheese bakes in this library (~35-45 min until set and golden, standard for this batter size); confirm exact time/pan size if available. Feta 5% and Hemed-style cream cheese 5% taken as standard light Israeli soft-cheese densities. Estimate — no macros given in the post. An optimized variant (whole-spelt flour, less salt, veg folded in) is presented in chat; this base entry is left as posted.

serving_desc: ≈175 g slice (batch ÷8) — side or light main; 2 slices = a fuller meal

ingredients.note: swap to whole spelt for fiber (see optimized version)
caramelized onion, oregano, broccoli, corn, spinach, etc. — the poster's own suggestion

steps: Whisk the eggs; mix in the cottage, white cheese, flour and baking powder.
Fold in the yellow cheese, feta and cream cheese (and any optional veg/herbs you're adding).
Pour into a greased/lined baking dish.

Bake at 180 °C, top-bottom heat, until set and golden on top (method caption cut off after this point — bake similarly to the library's other egg-cheese bakes, ~35-45 min, until a knife comes out clean; check your pan size).

batch_totals.note: Whole bake (8 slices), BASE recipe (no veg add-in). Four cheeses + 4 eggs drive protein and calcium hard, but feta (salty, brined) is the dominant sodium and fat source, and with no vegetables the dish has almost no fiber or folate — the opposite profile of the broccoli pashtida in this library.

him.verdict: Very high protein density for a baked dish — ~12.8 g protein for only 131 kcal (~9.8 g protein per 100 kcal, among the best in your library) from 4 eggs + 4 cheeses. The catch: as posted it's a cheese-only bake with essentially zero fiber and a heavy sodium load, almost entirely from the 250 g of feta (feta is a brined cheese — salty by nature even at '5%' fat). It's an excellent protein source, just nutritionally one-note without the vegetables the poster herself suggests adding.
flags: ~12.8 g protein / 131 kcal slice (~9.8 g protein per 100 kcal — excellent)
very high sodium (~430 mg/slice; ~3,440 mg batch) — feta is the main driver
almost no fiber (~0.1 g) or folate — no vegetables in the base list
moderate saturated fat (~4 g/slice) from 4 cheeses
white-flour binder is a small refined-carb contributor
suggested_mods: Take the poster's own suggestion: fold in a vegetable (spinach/broccoli/onion) — turns this from a protein-only dish into a real folate + fiber contributor
Rinse or soak the feta briefly, or cut it to ~180-200 g, to pull sodium down without losing the tang
Swap the 2 tbsp flour to whole spelt — small change, some fiber
No added salt needed anywhere — feta alone covers it

her_preconception.verdict: Good protein, choline (4 eggs) and calcium (4 cheeses), but as posted — with no vegetables — it's missing her top preconception nutrient (folate) almost entirely, and the sodium load from 250 g of feta is worth moderating in pregnancy. Feta is also a brined cheese: fully baked here, which is considered safe (cooked), but verify it's pasteurized. This is a dish that goes from fine to genuinely good for her the moment the optional spinach/broccoli get added — see the optimized version.
prenatal_highlights: fully baked, considered safe when cooked through

safety_advisories.note: Feta is a brined cheese — Listeria risk unless pasteurized. It's baked through here (cooked = considered safe); verify it's a pasteurized feta.
safety_advisories.swap: verify pasteurized, or use more cottage/white cheese in its place

suggested_mods: Fold in spinach or broccoli — turns this into a real folate source, which the base recipe lacks entirely
Keep sodium in mind — moderate the feta amount
Serve with tomato/pepper for vitamin C

cooking_guide: Whisk the eggs well, then stir in the cottage cheese, white cheese, flour and baking powder until smooth.
Fold in the chopped yellow cheese, crumbled feta and cream cheese — if you're adding any vegetables (spinach, broccoli, sautéed onion, corn), fold them in now too, well-drained if they were cooked.
Pour into a greased or lined baking dish and level the top.
Bake at 180 °C with top-bottom heat until the center is set (not wobbly) and the top is golden — check around 35 min and continue in 5-min increments; a knife in the middle should come out clean.
Rest 10 min before slicing so it holds together.
Tip: because feta and the yellow cheese are both salty, taste the raw batter before considering any extra salt — you almost certainly won't need it.
